Critique of political economy or simply the first critique of economy is a form of social critique that rejects the conventional ways of distributing resources. The critique also rejects what its advocates believe are unrealistic axioms , flawed historical assumptions, [ 1 ] and taking conventional economic mechanisms as a given [ 2 ] [ 3 ] or as transhistorical (true for all human societies for all time). [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The critique asserts the conventional economy is merely one of many types of historically specific ways to distribute resources, which emerged along with modernity (post-Renaissance Western society). [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ]
